title: TCS Wins Technology Partnership for JFK Airport's $19 Billion New Terminal One
excerpt: India's largest IT company will build the AI-driven digital backbone for New York's flagship international terminal, deploying its Cognix and ignio platforms across all operations.
body:
• Tata Consultancy Services has been named the technology and innovation partner for New Terminal One at JFK Airport, part of the Port Authority's $19 billion redevelopment
  • TCS will build the terminal's digital backbone, managing passenger processing, AI-driven operations, baggage handling, cybersecurity, and infrastructure systems
  • The company will deploy its proprietary Cognix and ignio platforms to provide real-time visibility across all terminal operations
  • The partnership aims for a five-star Skytrax rating and positions an Indian IT company at the center of America's largest airport transformation

India's IT Giant Takes on New York's Biggest Airport Project

Tata Consultancy Services has secured one of its most high-profile American contracts, landing the role of technology and innovation partner for New Terminal One at John F. Kennedy International Airport. The deal, disclosed in regulatory filings to BSE and NSE on July 14, places India's largest IT services firm at the center of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey's $19 billion transformation of JFK into a world-class international gateway.

TCS will be responsible for building the terminal's entire digital infrastructure — from passenger processing and baggage handling systems to AI-powered operations management and cybersecurity. The scope is comprehensive: the Indian company will effectively run the technology stack of what is designed to become New York's flagship international terminal.

AI and Real-Time Operations

The company plans to deploy its proprietary Cognix and ignio platforms, which combine artificial intelligence with predictive analytics to give terminal operators and partner airlines real-time visibility across every aspect of airport operations. The system will monitor passenger flows, baggage logistics, security protocols, and IT infrastructure, identifying problems before they affect travelers.

— Jennifer Aument, CEO of New Terminal One

Amit Bajaj, TCS's President for North America, described the deal as part of a broader shift in how airports operate. "Airports are increasingly evolving into technology-driven ecosystems where AI plays a key role in improving operations and personalising passenger services," Bajaj said. "Our partnership with New Terminal One is about helping build that future."

A Five-Star Ambition

The New Terminal One is the centerpiece of JFK's largest overhaul in decades. The redevelopment includes two new terminals, modernization of two existing ones, a new ground transportation center, and a redesigned roadway network. Aument said the project is targeting a five-star Skytrax rating, which would place it among the world's elite airport facilities.

TCS's involvement extends beyond pure technology deployment. The partnership includes terminal infrastructure management, enterprise application support, and ongoing innovation — essentially embedding TCS into the terminal's operations for the long term. Airlines operating from the terminal are expected to benefit through lower operating costs enabled by better monitoring and automated processes.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the millions of Indian Americans and NRIs who transit through JFK each year, the partnership carries a distinctive significance: a Tata company will be powering the systems behind their airport experience. JFK handles tens of millions of international passengers annually, and the India-US corridor is one of the busiest long-haul routes in the world.

The contract also underscores TCS's position in the global technology services market. Despite a challenging year for the Indian IT sector — TCS shares have declined roughly 32% year-to-date — the company reported consolidated revenues exceeding $30 billion for the fiscal year ending March 2026. High-visibility contracts like the JFK deal help demonstrate capability to prospective clients in an increasingly competitive market.

The partnership will be supported by TCS's Travel, Transport, and Hospitality business unit, which works with airlines, airports, and logistics companies across the world to modernize operations using AI, cloud technologies, and advanced analytics.
